text:
Marta K: Quick question — do we expose backpressure controls on the SDK or keep it strictly a transport concern? thinking about Python/TS/Go parity.

Samir: leaning transport-only. keep SDK surface minimal. expose a couple top-level config knobs but let transports implement semaphores.

Jordan: +1 on minimal surface but we need sane defaults and hooks for metrics. users will hit OOMs if we just leave it to them.

Olivia: For streaming-heavy flows, having an SDK-level backpressure helper is handy so user code can `await`/`pause` reads instead of juggling buffers. Node streams have natural primitives for this.

Ryan: For Go, want `Acquire(ctx)` style semaphore so cancellation propagates. any blocking should be context-aware.

Samir: Proposal sketch: transport interface supports an optional BackpressureHandler. SDKs register a default impl (language-native). config keys: `max_concurrent`, `buffer_strategy` = ('drop_oldest'|'block'|'unbounded'), plus `prefetch` for iterators.

Marta K: How does this interact with pagination? If SDK auto-paginates, backpressure semantics get weird (prefetch may inadvertently fetch many pages).

Jordan: We should avoid aggressive auto-pagination for streaming results. Provide an iterator/stream helper that respects backpressure and exposes `prefetch`. Default should be 1.

Olivia: Example TS UX: 
```ts
const it = client.responses.stream({ model, prompt, page_size: 50, prefetch: 2 });
for await (const page of it) {
  // process page - backpressure respected by SDK
}
```

Samir: Mirror in Python with async iterator and also provide a blocking sync iterator backed by a bounded queue thread. Keep sync path memory-bounded by default.

Ryan: Go transport sketch: 
```go
type Transport interface {
  Send(ctx context.Context, req *Request) (*Response, error)
  Stream(ctx context.Context, req *Request, out chan<- *Chunk) error
  Acquire(ctx context.Context) error // optional, detected by interface assertion
}
```

Marta K: Are we comfortable making `Acquire` optional? worried about third-party transports.

Samir: Make it optional. if not implemented, SDK wraps the transport with a token-bucket/semaphore fallback. keep the ABI small.

Jordan: Testing + perf: add unit tests for bursty clients, e2e for high-seq-length streaming, and a perf harness to tune `max_concurrent` defaults per model class.

Olivia: Docs/workflows: show recommended presets (chat low-latency, embed high-throughput). include migration guide for users who rely on current implicit buffering.

dev-bot: New RFC-ish PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/512

Marta K: Action items: Samir -> draft transport interface PR; Jordan -> iterator helper + tests; Olivia -> docs + examples; Ryan -> prototype Go sem and sample impl. Sync in eng-sync next Wed to align defaults.

Ryan: +1

Samir: I'll try to open the PR by EOD Thursday.

Marta K: thanks all :thumbsup:
